antipatterns: bootstrap/app.php:27-31 rewrites every 404 HttpException (including any deliberate abort(404, 'custom message')) to a fixed 'Not found.'. The broad catch hides internals but also drops intentional messages.
tests/Feature/OrdersApiTest.php:20-34 checks newest-first by comparing ISO strings collected from created_at. It works, but asserting the expected IDs in order would be clearer.
tests/Feature/OrdersApiTest.php:61 `not->toContain('Order')` is a blunt string check.
strengths: Only implementation that handles middleware order: `prependToPriorityList(SubstituteBindings::class, CheckAbilities::class)` makes ability checks run before route-model binding. A token without orders:read therefore gets 403 for both missing and foreign order IDs. My probe confirmed it, so there is no existence oracle.
OrderPolicy uses Response::denyAsNotFound() with `$order->user()->is($user)`, wired through `can:view,order`. That is the idiomatic way to return 404 for another user's order.
The global 404 renderer closes the `No query results for model [App\Models\Order]` leak. Missing, foreign and non-numeric IDs all return the same `{"message":"Not found."}`.
Modern model: #[Fillable] attribute, a casts() method with an integer cast (a string '42' comes back as 42), and a typed HasMany/BelongsTo.
Uses `latest()->latest('id')` as a stable tiebreaker, plus a composite (user_id, created_at) index.

Tests send real bearer tokens, with forgetGuards so a cached guard can't hide a bad token. They cover requests with no Accept header, the ability matrix including a 403 for a missing ID, a datasets-driven validation suite, duplicate references across users, user_id mass-assignment, and a debug-off leak check across 401/403/404/405.

bugs: Order has no integer cast for total_cents (app/Models/Order.php). A client posting total_cents='42' gets a 201 body with "total_cents":"42" (a string), while GET returns an int, so the API's type contract is inconsistent.

app/Http/Controllers/Api/OrderController.php:23 takes `string $order` and calls findOrFail on the relation instead of using route-model binding plus a policy. It works and is safe, but it moves authorization into the query and skips the framework's policy layer.
tests/Feature/OrdersApiTest.php:134-141: the test name says 'unknown API routes 404' but it sends DELETE to an existing path and asserts `toBeIn([404, 405])`, which is non-committal.
tests/Feature/OrdersApiTest.php:12 calls Http::preventStrayRequests() although nothing makes HTTP calls.
tests/Feature/OrdersApiTest.php:15 tokenFor doesn't reset auth guards. That is safe in these tests but fragile if a test ever switches users.
strengths: Scoped lookup with `$request->user()->orders()->findOrFail($order)`. With no route binding, ability middleware always runs first: a token without the ability gets 403 for both missing and foreign IDs (verified).
The NotFoundHttpException renderer turns the leaky model-not-found message into a uniform 'Not found.'.
Uses a FormRequest, a resource, `latest()->latest('id')` and #[Fillable].

Tests run with debug off and use an expectNoInternals helper on 401/403/404/422 bodies. A dataset-driven ability matrix uses raw call() with no Accept header, and the validation dataset includes a duplicate reference.

bugs: Route-model binding (SubstituteBindings in the api group) runs before CheckAbilities on GET /api/orders/{order}. A token without orders:read gets 404 for a nonexistent ID but 403 for an existing order owned by someone else (probe: 403 vs 404). That breaks 'a token without the ability gets 403' and leaks whether other users' order IDs exist, enumerable by any token holder.

bootstrap/app.php:19 `redirectGuestsTo(fn () => null)` applies app-wide, so web routes also lose login redirects. There is no web auth here, so the impact is small, but the change is broader than the API.
antipatterns: bootstrap/app.php:22 registers an unused 'ability' => CheckForAnyAbility alias.

app/Http/Requests/StoreOrderRequest.php:13 adds max:4294967295 to match the unsignedInteger column. That is defensible, but an unsignedInteger column for money in cents caps orders at about $42.9M for no clear reason.
tests/Feature/OrdersApiTest.php:9 calls Http::preventStrayRequests() although nothing makes HTTP calls.
tests/Feature/OrdersApiTest.php:36-37 tests the 403 only against the user's own order, so the binding-order bug goes untested.
strengths: Clean policy with denyAsNotFound plus `can:view,order`; the integer cast, #[Fillable] and `latest()->latest('id')` match impl-1.
A concise HttpExceptionInterface renderer gives a uniform 'Not found.' for all API 404s.
The validation rule matches the column range, so oversized totals return 422 instead of a DB error.

Best-organised tests: describe blocks, a dataset for unauthenticated requests on every route, explicit no-Accept tests for 200/201/403/422, validation datasets asserting messages, and a debug-off server-error test that drops the table and asserts 'Server Error' with no SQLSTATE.

v.rationale:
I ranked impl-1 first, impl-2 second and impl-3 third. All three test suites pass (19, 19 and 29 tests). All three already return JSON for api/* routes and replace Laravel's leaky "No query results for model [App\Models\Order]" 404 message with a uniform "Not found.". Debug-off probes found no internals in the 401, 403, 404, 405 or 422 responses of any of them.

The deciding probe was a token without orders:read requesting another user's order versus a missing one.
- **impl-1:** returns 403 for both, because it explicitly puts CheckAbilities ahead of SubstituteBindings in the priority list.
- **impl-2:** also returns 403 for both, because it skips route-model binding and uses a scoped findOrFail.
- **impl-3:** returns 403 for the existing foreign order and 404 for the missing one. That breaks the 403 requirement and lets any token holder probe whether other users' order IDs exist. This is a real bug in the task's focus area.

impl-2's only bug is cosmetic: with no integer cast, a string total_cents is echoed back as a string in the 201 response. It also has some sloppiness: an unused alias, a vague 404/405 test, and a pointless Http::preventStrayRequests() call.

impl-1 combines the most idiomatic design (a policy with denyAsNotFound, the integer cast, #[Fillable], a stable sort tiebreaker) with the middleware-ordering fix and solid tests, including a 403 check on a missing ID.

impl-3 has the best-organised tests but ranks last because of the ability-ordering bug.
